title: The mobile "compact" /api/data view is 13.0% LARGER than the desktop "array" view, so phones and low-memory devices are deliberately routed to the heavier payload
claimUnderTest: server.py:3126-3128 — 'Mobile / slow-network view — prune ~20 audit + trust fields. ~90% byte reduction.'  frontend/lib/device-profile.js:84 — 'Mobile / slow network -> "compact"'.  frontend/app/api/dynasty-data/route.js:45 — 'mobile / slow-network callers ask for the compact (~90% smaller) view'.
observed: compact serves 7,363,760 raw bytes; array serves 6,514,536; app serves 5,818,304; full serves 11,953,535.  compact is 849,224 bytes (+13.04%) LARGER than the view desktop asks for, and only 38.4% smaller than full — not 90%.  Mechanism, byte-accounted: view=array drops the legacy `players` dict entirely and ships playersArray only (6,132,969 b, 55 fields/row).  view=compact prunes 14 audit fields per row (55->41, playersArray 6,132,969 -> 3,659,280 b) but then ALSO ships the legacy `players` dict (3,336,826 b) — the same 1,092 rows encoded twice.  The per-row pruning is real and works; shipping both encodings more than cancels it.  Confirmed end-to-end in a real browser: desktop /rankings transferred 1,040,158 b / decoded 11,767,159 b; the same page at 390px transferred 1,135,662 b / decoded 12,553,077 b — mobile pays 95,504 more compressed bytes and 785,918 more decoded bytes.  isMobileProfile() also returns true for any device reporting navigator.deviceMemory <= 4, so budget laptops take the heavy path too.

reproduction.command: for v in '' '?view=app' '?view=array' '?view=compact'; do printf '%-16s raw=%s\n' "${v:-full}" $(curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w '%{size_download}' "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data$v"); done
reproduction.expected: compact <= array (a view named 'compact' and routed to the weakest devices should be the smallest non-degenerate view)

numericProof.formula: delta = compactTotalBytes - arrayTotalBytes ; pctLarger = 100*delta/arrayTotalBytes ; claimedReduction = 1 - compactTotalBytes/fullTotalBytes

userImpact: A user on a phone or a 4 GB laptop downloads 95 KB more over the wire and parses 785 KB more JSON on every page load than the same user on a desktop, on a product whose stated design goal is 'mobile-friendly'. On a 3G connection the extra compressed bytes alone add roughly 0.5-1 s to first usable board.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A01-F17 established that desktop requests view=array and therefore has no legacy `players` dict, contradicting CLAUDE.md. This finding is the byte consequence on the OTHER side of that split: compact still carries the dict, which is exactly why it is bigger. PRIOR-A01-F08 is the correctness side of the same view (compact prunes four fields the rankings UI reads); the two are independent and both stand.

whatWorks: The per-row compaction itself is correct and effective — 55 fields to 41, playersArray 6.13 MB to 3.66 MB. view=array's decision to drop the legacy dict is the right one. ETag + If-None-Match revalidation works on all views (304 in 3 ms, 0 bytes).
rootCause: src/api/compact_view.py applies field pruning to BOTH `playersArray` and the legacy `players` dict, and the compact builder retains the dict, whereas the array builder deletes it. The compact view therefore ships two pruned encodings of the same 1,092 rows where array ships one unpruned encoding of one.
requiredRepair: Delete the legacy `players` dict from the compact payload (it is what array already does) — that alone takes compact to ~4.03 MB, 38% below array and 66% below full, which is closer to the '~90%' the comments claim than anything shipping today. Then correct the three '~90% byte reduction' / '~90% smaller' comments to the measured figure.
dependencies: Requires confirming no compact-view consumer reads the legacy dict; frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js::buildRows prefers playersArray when present, and view=array already proves the dict-free shape renders.

title: AppShell fetches the full multi-megabyte player contract on EVERY private page — including a 404 page and pages that never render a player row
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md 'Performance Rules' — 'Reduce blocking work on initial load', 'Eliminate duplicated calculations, repeated fetches, oversized payloads'. AppShell.jsx:33 declares exactly one exemption from the private data fetch, PUBLIC_ONLY_ROUTE_PREFIXES = ['/league'], and that exemption exists for a SECURITY reason (leaking private rankings to public visitors), not a performance one.
observed: Measured in a real browser through request interception, 13 of the 14 pages probed issue GET /api/dynasty-data?view=array|compact and decode 11.7-13.1 MB.  The only page that does not is /league, which is exempt for security.  Pages that fetch the whole 1,092-row board while rendering none of it: /news (12,533,315 b decoded), /bdvm (12,488,678), /market/sharp-roster-percentage (12,481,120), /league-comparison (12,560,784), /waivers (12,578,490), /settings (12,505,629).  /terminal — which is a Next 404, 'This page could not be found.' — still decodes 12,481,320 bytes.  The fetch is unconditional in PrivateAppShell (AppShell.jsx:61) because global search and the player popup want `rows`; the actual index those two need is name + id + position + value, roughly 90 KB for 1,092 rows.

reproduction.expected: pages with no player board (/news, /bdvm, /league-comparison, /market/*, and a 404) do not download the player board
reproduction.actual: all of them download 12.4-12.6 MB decoded

numericProof.formula: wastedDecodedBytes_per_page_without_a_board = decodedBytes - (bytes actually rendered); for /terminal (a 404) the rendered board bytes are 0

userImpact: Opening /news to read three headlines, or /bdvm to see a 'no snapshot yet' message, costs the user a full board download and JSON parse. On mobile this is the dominant cost of every navigation in the app and it is paid before anything on the page can render its own data. A mistyped URL that lands on the 404 page costs 1.0 MB over the wire.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the app-shell-level unconditional contract fetch. PRIOR-A01-F17 and PRIOR-A01-F08 concern which VIEW is fetched, not that it is fetched everywhere.

whatWorks: The fetch itself is well engineered: single request per page, zero duplicate URLs measured across all 28 page/viewport combinations, ETag revalidation with 304 support, gzip, and a stream-through Next bridge with an idle-abort timeout. The /league security exemption is correctly implemented and correctly motivated.
rootCause: AppShell.jsx:61 calls useDynastyData() unconditionally in PrivateAppShell. The only gate (isPublicOnlyRoute) was added for data-leak reasons; no route-level gate exists for 'this page has no board'.
requiredRepair: Either (a) split useDynastyData into a lightweight search-index fetch (name/playerId/position/rankDerivedValue) that AppShell always makes and a full-board fetch that only board-rendering pages opt into, or (b) invert the gate so pages declare `needsBoard` and AppShell defers the full fetch until one does. Option (a) preserves global search on every page at ~1.5% of the current bytes.
dependencies: Needs a new lightweight backend view (or reuse of ?view=startup narrowed further). Interacts with W26-F001 — fix that first so whichever view remains is the smallest.

title: /draft downloads the full 11.95 MB /api/data contract to read a 46.8 KB list of 12 team names, from three separate call sites, two of them with cache: "no-store"
claimUnderTest: server.py:8324-8329 records that /api/draft-capital was already fixed once for exactly this class of problem — '/draft calling it three times per page load'. The contract fetch on the same page was not covered by that fix.
observed: /draft issues BOTH `/api/data?leagueKey=dynasty_main` (no `view` param, so the backend serves the FULL 11,953,535-byte contract) AND `/api/dynasty-data?view=array` (6,514,536 b), plus `/api/data` bare from a third call site. Browser-measured totals for /draft: desktop decoded 23,849,422 b / transferred 2,216,644 b; mobile decoded 24,571,176 b / transferred 2,312,148 b — roughly double every other page in the app. All three /api/data call sites consume only `data.sleeper.teams`, which is 46,792 bytes of the 11,953,535 served — 0.39%. Two of the three pass `cache: "no-store"`, which defeats both the browser HTTP cache and the ETag/304 path the backend already implements, so the bytes are re-fetched on every mount and every sync-preview click.

reproduction.expected: the page fetches roughly the bytes it consumes

userImpact: Opening the live draft board — the one page a user loads under time pressure, mid-auction, often on a phone on venue wifi — costs twice the bytes of any other page. Clicking 'Sync rookies' re-downloads the full 11.95 MB contract again because that call site is cache:no-store.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A00-* findings on /draft concern bid arithmetic, not payload. The /api/draft-capital triple-fetch on this page was fixed previously (server.py:8324); the contract triple-fetch beside it was not.

whatWorks: The parallelisation in fetchSyncPreview (Promise.all over /api/data and /api/draft-capital) is correct — those two are genuinely independent and are not serialised. The cancellation guard on the mount effect is correct.
rootCause: Three call sites want `sleeper.teams` and there is no narrow endpoint that serves it, so each reaches for the whole contract. None passes a `view` param, so each gets the widest view the backend has.
requiredRepair: Add `?view=startup` (or a new teams-only view) to the three call sites — that alone halves the cost — and hoist the three fetches into one memoised call keyed on selectedLeagueKey. Drop `cache: "no-store"` so the backend's existing ETag/304 does its job. Best fix: serve `sleeper.teams` from the existing /api/leagues response, which already carries per-league roster settings and would make the contract fetch unnecessary here.

title: GET /api/bdvm/roster spends 48 seconds on nflverse downloads that the very next function call discards, because the code already knows there is no projection snapshot before it starts fetching
claimUnderTest: src/api/bdvm_api.py module docstring — 'Thin, cached bridge... Player context (nflverse id map + career loads) and the season schedule are fetched lazily'. AUDIT_PROTOCOL pre-declares 'data/bdvm/ does not exist -> Blocked by data', so the 'no snapshot' ANSWER is not the finding; the 48 seconds spent producing it is.
observed: bdvm_api.py:177 computes `snapshot = latest_snapshot_path(season)` and gets None. On a cache miss it nonetheless calls `_context_for(season)` (line 200) and `_schedule_for(season)` (line 201) before `run_valuation`. run_valuation returns `no_projection_snapshot` at service.py:305 — before it reads `context` (first used line 338/453) or `schedule_weeks` (line 622). Every byte fetched is discarded. Measured cost: the shared route probe recorded 47,994 ms for a 310-byte response on the cold path; re-run in a fresh process against an already-warm nfl_data disk cache the same two calls still cost 8.69 s (schedule 1.27 s, context 7.41 s, 23,934 context players built and thrown away). The 48 s figure is the cold cost of downloading the nflverse id map (24.7 MB), six seasons of weekly stats (357.4 MB) and six seasons of snap counts (51.4 MB). Sibling routes /api/bdvm/values and /api/bdvm/trades measured 6 ms and 5 ms in the same probe run purely because /api/bdvm/roster (alphabetically first) had already paid and warmed the per-process _context_cache / _schedule_cache. schedule.py additionally retries a second 60 s-timeout URL on failure, so the schedule leg alone can block 120 s.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import time;from src.bdvm.projections import latest_snapshot_path;from src.bdvm.actuals import nfl_projection_season;s=nfl_projection_season();print('snapshot',latest_snapshot_path(s));t=time.time();from src.bdvm.schedule import fetch_team_weeks;fetch_team_weeks(s);a=time.time()-t;t=time.time();from src.bdvm.context import fetch_and_build_context;c=fetch_and_build_context(s);print('schedule_s',round(a,2),'context_s',round(time.time()-t,2),'players',len(c))"
reproduction.expected: 0 s — with snapshot None the engine has nothing to value
reproduction.actual: snapshot None ; schedule_s 1.27 ; context_s 7.41 ; players 23934  (47,994 ms on a cold nfl_data cache)

numericProof.formula: wastedSeconds = scheduleSeconds + contextSeconds, given latest_snapshot_path(season) is None at bdvm_api.py:177 and run_valuation returns at service.py:305 before either value is read

userImpact: The first user to open /bdvm after any process restart waits 48 seconds for a message that says 'no projection snapshot' — information the server had in under a millisecond. In production WITH a snapshot the same 48 s is still paid on the first request after every deploy, and it holds an anyio threadpool worker (of 40) for the whole duration.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A15-F16 flagged that get_bdvm_values' cache key contains id(contract), a reusable CPython address — I confirm that line is still present (bdvm_api.py:180). This finding is a different defect in the same function: the ordering of the snapshot check against the two network fetches.

whatWorks: The refusal itself is exemplary — the engine returns status no_projection_snapshot with an actionable message and does not fabricate projections, exactly as the module contract promises. The LRU sizing rationale (_VALUES_CACHE_MAX=4, bdvm_api.py:36-40) is well reasoned. The 'failed actuals fetch is returned but never memoized' rule (lines 143-153) is a genuinely good cache-poisoning guard.
rootCause: The snapshot existence check lives inside run_valuation (service.py:303) while the two expensive enrichment fetches live in the caller (bdvm_api.py:200-201). The caller already computes the same snapshot path at line 177 for its cache key, so it has the information it needs to skip.
requiredRepair: Three lines: after `snapshot = latest_snapshot_path(season)` at bdvm_api.py:177, if snapshot is None pass `context={}` and `schedule_weeks=None` straight through instead of calling _context_for / _schedule_for. Separately, drop schedule.py's second 60 s-timeout attempt to a much shorter budget — a 120 s worst case on an optional enrichment is not a sane bound for a request path.

title: Three of the slowest cold paths have no stampede protection: concurrent misses each run the full multi-second build
claimUnderTest: The repo demonstrably knows this pattern: server.py implements per-key asyncio single-flight for _OVERLAY_RESPONSE_CACHE (line 2960), _OVERRIDES_RESPONSE_CACHE (line 3011), _DRAFT_CAPITAL_CACHE (line 8375) and _heavy_section_cache (line 8758), and src/api/sleeper_overlay.py:_BUILD_LOCKS documents 'before these locks concurrent expirees each launched their own storm'.
observed: Four caches on the slowest measured routes hold their lock only across the dict get/put, never across the build.  (1) bdvm_api._context_for / _schedule_for release _aux_lock before fetching, so N concurrent cold /api/bdvm/* requests each launch a full nflverse download (433 MB per attempt, measured 47,994 ms).  (2) bdvm_api.get_bdvm_values releases _lock at line 197 and re-acquires at 214, so N concurrent misses each run run_valuation.  (3) league_comparison.service.build_comparison has a 7-day DISK cache and no lock at all — cold cost measured 26,577 ms in the route probe; N concurrent cold requests each load every nflverse season and recompute.  (4) gameplan.get_league_bundle holds _CACHE_LOCK only around the dict lookup while its own docstring says 'only the ~1.35 s solve is cached'.

reproduction.command: grep -n 'with _aux_lock' -A3 src/api/bdvm_api.py | sed -n '1,20p'   # lock released before the fetch on lines 64-70 and 80-86; compare server.py:2958-2996 which holds an asyncio.Lock across the whole encode
reproduction.expected: the build runs inside the lock, or a per-key single-flight lock exists
reproduction.actual: lock scope covers only the dict access; the multi-second build runs unlocked

numericProof.formula: worst-case work on a cold cache = N * coldMs instead of 1 * coldMs; with bdvm at 47,994 ms and 40 threadpool workers, 40 concurrent cold /api/bdvm/* requests saturate the entire pool for ~48 s

userImpact: A cold restart plus a handful of simultaneous users (or one user with several tabs) multiplies the 48 s / 27 s cold costs instead of sharing them, and can occupy every threadpool worker so unrelated endpoints queue behind it.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers stampede protection. Rated medium rather than high because I could not safely generate concurrent cold misses under the audit's read-only rule (it would force real outbound nflverse fetches); the claim rests on the lock scope in source plus the measured single-request cold costs.

whatWorks: Four other caches in this codebase get this exactly right, with the reasoning written down: _OVERLAY_RESPONSE_CACHE / _OVERRIDES_RESPONSE_CACHE (per-key asyncio.Lock, re-check inside the lock, held locks preserved across eviction), _DRAFT_CAPITAL_CACHE (per-league asyncio.Lock with post-wait re-check), _heavy_section_cache (waiters block on the loop, not in the threadpool, so they do not hold worker tokens hostage), and sleeper_overlay._BUILD_LOCKS. The public-league cache goes further with stale-while-revalidate, a suppression flag on the background refresh thread, and hit/miss/stale counters.
rootCause: These four caches were written as plain memoisation ('check dict, else compute, else store') without adopting the single-flight pattern the same repo uses elsewhere.
requiredRepair: Port the existing pattern: a per-key lock dict, acquire it on miss, re-check inside, compute, store, release. For bdvm_api use threading.Lock (the work runs in a threadpool worker); for league_comparison the same; for gameplan widen _CACHE_LOCK to cover the solve or add a per-league build lock.

title: GET /api/player/{id}/realized re-reads and re-parses a 61.7 MB JSON file and linearly scans 19,421 rows on every single request, with no in-process memoisation
claimUnderTest: src/nfl_data/cache.py module docstring — 'We don't want to hammer nflverse on every request... so every ingest call goes through this cache.' The cache prevents network hammering; it does not prevent disk-and-CPU hammering, and nothing above it memoises.
observed: The handler calls `_ing.fetch_weekly_stats([2025, 2026])` per request. That resolves to a DISK-only TTL cache — `cache.get()` does `json.loads(data_path.read_text())` with no in-process layer — so every call re-reads and re-parses the 61,706,838-byte cache entry for key `weekly_stats:2025,2026` and materialises 19,421 dict rows. The handler then filters those 19,421 rows with a Python list comprehension to find one player's GSIS id. Measured directly: 0.762 s for the first fetch and 0.745 s for an immediately-repeated fetch in the same process — no memoisation at any level. End-to-end route latency, repeated 5x: 5.179 s (cold) then 1.136 / 0.954 / 0.915 / 0.840 s. The steady state is ~0.8 s of pure server CPU per player popup. PlayerPopup fires this on every popup open (client-side 30-minute cache is per playerId only), so a user browsing 20 players costs ~16 s of server CPU and ~1.2 GB of JSON parsing.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import time;from src.nfl_data import ingest;t=time.time();r=ingest.fetch_weekly_stats([2025,2026]);print('rows',len(r),'first_s',round(time.time()-t,3));t=time.time();ingest.fetch_weekly_stats([2025,2026]);print('second_s',round(time.time()-t,3))" ; for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do curl -s -o /dev/null -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -w '%{time_total}\n' 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/player/4046/realized'; done
reproduction.expected: second in-process fetch is ~0 s (memoised); route steady state well under 100 ms
reproduction.actual: rows 19421 first_s 0.762 second_s 0.745 ; route steady state 0.79-0.95 s

numericProof.formula: serverSecondsPerSession = routeSteadyStateSeconds * popupsPerBrowsingSession ; bytesParsedPerSession = cacheFileBytes * popupsPerBrowsingSession

userImpact: Every player popup that reaches the realized-points section stalls ~0.8 s server-side, and the cost is per-player rather than per-session, so it scales linearly with browsing. Under concurrent users each request also allocates ~60 MB of transient Python objects.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A21-F16 and PRIOR-A22-F02 both concern the CORRECTNESS of this route (wrong league's scoring; IDP players return zero weeks). Neither touches the per-request 61.7 MB re-parse. Independent.

whatWorks: The client-side cache in PlayerPopup (_realizedCache, 30-minute TTL keyed by sleeperId, with negative caching on failure) is correct and does real work. The handler's row-filter comment documenting the player_id vs player_id_gsis bug is exactly the kind of note that prevents a regression.
rootCause: src/nfl_data/cache.py is a disk-only TTL cache with no in-process layer, and no caller adds one. A request-scoped or process-scoped memo of the parsed rows was never introduced because the cache's docstring frames the problem as network hammering only.
requiredRepair: Add an in-process memo above the disk cache keyed on (cache key, file mtime_ns) so the parse happens once per process per refresh. Separately, build a GSIS-id index once instead of a 19,421-row linear scan per player — that turns the filter from O(n) per request into O(1).

title: The nfl_data disk cache has no last-known-good fallback, no size bound (590 MB today), and stores three byte-identical copies of the same 61.7 MB file under three keys
claimUnderTest: cache.py:1-15 — 'TTL file cache for NFL data pulls... every ingest call goes through this cache.' ingest.py:315-330 — on a stale entry the fetch is retried and, if it returns None, `return []` — the still-present, still-parseable cached file is not consulted.
observed: Three distinct defects in one cache.  (a) NO LAST-KNOWN-GOOD: cache.get() returns None the instant `(now - fetched_at) > ttl_seconds` (line 84) and every ingest wrapper then returns [] if the refetch fails. A 24h+1s-old, perfectly usable 61.7 MB file on disk is ignored, so a transient nflverse outage turns /api/player/{id}/realized into a 200 with `reason: "no_stats_available"` and every ROS/BDVM consumer into an empty result — from full data to no data with no intermediate degradation.  (b) NO SIZE BOUND: there is no prune, no LRU, no total-bytes cap — the only unlink() calls are for corrupt entries and explicit evict(key). Measured today: 590 MB across 7 entries, the largest a single 357,376,944-byte JSON.  (c) DUPLICATE STORAGE: keys are the sorted YEAR LIST, so `weekly_stats:2025` and `weekly_stats:2025,2026` are md5-identical (071b2583...) because 2026 has no rows yet; and `weekly_def_stats:2025` is the SAME md5 again, because nflverse_direct maps both `weekly_stats` and `weekly_defensive_stats` to one unified URL (documented at nflverse_direct.py:82-83). That is 185,120,514 bytes — 31% of the cache — holding three copies of one file.

reproduction.command: cd data/nfl_data_cache && for f in *.meta.json; do d=${f%.meta.json}.json; k=$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('$f'))['key'])"); echo "$(md5sum $d|cut -c1-32) $(stat -c%s $d) $k"; done | sort ; du -sh data/nfl_data_cache
reproduction.expected: distinct keys hold distinct content; total cache size bounded
reproduction.actual: 071b2583811fc9a3dbad5ad156a4be9c appears for weekly_def_stats:2025, weekly_stats:2025 and weekly_stats:2025,2026 (61,706,838 b each); total 590M

userImpact: On the (b) axis, an unattended production box accumulates nflverse snapshots until the disk fills, at which point cache.put() raises and the ingest flow breaks. On the (a) axis, the day nflverse is briefly unreachable after a TTL expiry, several surfaces flip from correct data to honest-but-empty in one step, when a 25-hour-old snapshot would have been almost exactly as good.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the nfl_data cache layer itself.

whatWorks: Atomic-ish writes (tempfile + rename) are correct and prevent a crashed process from wedging the cache. Corrupt-entry self-eviction on both the meta and data paths is correct. JSON rather than pickle for portability is the right call and is justified in the docstring. The put() failure path deliberately swallows so a full disk does not kill ingest.
rootCause: cache.get() implements a hard TTL with no stale tier, cache.put() implements no accounting, and cache keys are derived from the caller's argument list rather than from the underlying resource, so two callers requesting overlapping year ranges of one file get separate full copies.
requiredRepair: (a) Add a `stale_ok` return path — get() returns (value, is_stale) and ingest wrappers serve stale on refetch failure with a staleness stamp on the payload, so the honest-empty state is reserved for 'we have never had this'. (b) Add a total-bytes budget with oldest-first eviction, checked in put(). (c) Key weekly stats per SEASON, not per year-list, and dedupe the offense/defense entries onto the single unified file the URL map already points both at.

title: An unauthenticated caller can force /api/draft-capital's full workbook+KTC+Sleeper rebuild every 300 s, and a failing KTC live fetch is never negative-cached so the cost recurs forever
claimUnderTest: server.py:8323-8336 — 'This endpoint used to run ~4s of synchronous work... Cache: key = league key; TTL = 300s'. The cache is real; what is not addressed is who is allowed to miss it and what a failing upstream costs.
observed: Two coupled defects.  (a) ANONYMOUS COLD BUILD: /api/draft-capital returns 200 to an unauthenticated caller (redacted, `rookieBoardRedacted: true`), but redaction happens per-response AFTER the build. So an anon client that polls every 5 minutes forces the full openpyxl workbook parse + KTC live fetch + up to six Sleeper calls on every TTL expiry. Measured anonymously with no cookie: 2.692 s, then 0.003 s, 0.004 s (cache hit) — and the shared route probe caught the genuinely cold first call at 13,188 ms.  (b) NO NEGATIVE CACHING ON KTC: `_get_ktc_rookies()` (server.py:7113) returns the 6h cache when fresh, else calls `_fetch_ktc_rookies_live()` (15 s urlopen timeout). On failure it falls through to `_parse_csv_rookies()` and returns those rows WITHOUT writing `_ktc_cache["fetched_at"]`. The failure is therefore never remembered: every subsequent draft-capital cache miss re-attempts the failing live scrape. That is the 2.692 s I measured — the KTC attempt timing out, once per 300 s, forever, in a production where KTC is blocked or rate-limiting.

reproduction.command: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'anon %{http_code} %{size_download}b %{time_total}s\n' 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/draft-capital'; done   # no cookie jar
reproduction.expected: anonymous callers cannot trigger a multi-second server-side build; a failing upstream is remembered

numericProof.formula: forcedRebuildsPerDayPerLeague = secondsPerDay / draftCapitalTtlSeconds ; serverSecondsPerDay = forcedRebuildsPerDayPerLeague * anonColdSeconds

userImpact: On a public deployment this is a free amplification vector: 288 forced rebuilds per day per league from an unauthenticated client, each holding a threadpool worker for 2.7-13.2 s. For the legitimate user, every /draft load that lands just after a TTL expiry pays the failing-KTC timeout instead of the 3 ms cache hit.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A00-F04 concerns the CORRECTNESS of the Sleeper-derived draft-capital board (fabricated pick values). This is the ingest/caching axis of the same endpoint and is independent of it. The anonymous 200 itself may be intentional public-board behaviour — the finding is the uncached COST behind it, not the exposure.

whatWorks: The per-league asyncio single-flight lock with a post-wait re-check (server.py:8375-8394) is correct and does prevent the /draft triple-fetch from fanning out. Redacting on a per-response copy rather than mutating the cached object (documented at 8337-8340) is exactly right and avoids a nasty cross-viewer leak. `ktcSource: "csv"` is honestly stamped on the response so a consumer can tell the live fetch failed.
rootCause: The 300 s TTL bounds staleness but not who may pay to refill it, and `_get_ktc_rookies` treats a failed live fetch as 'try again next time' rather than as a fact worth caching.
requiredRepair: On live-fetch failure, stamp `_ktc_cache` with the CSV rows and a shortened `fetched_at` (e.g. 15-minute backoff) so the failure is remembered — the CSV fallback is already the answer, so caching it costs nothing. Separately, serve anonymous callers only from an existing cache entry and return the last-known-good (or 503) rather than letting them trigger a build.

title: /api/bdvm/* and /api/valuation/league-adjusted send no Cache-Control and no ETag, so an expensive league-scoped payload is re-requested and re-sent on every navigation
claimUnderTest: Every other comparable route on this server sets an explicit policy: /api/data 'private, max-age=30, stale-while-revalidate=300' with an ETag; /api/terminal 'private, max-age=30, stale-while-revalidate=120'; /api/news 'public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=180'; /api/public/league 'public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300'; /api/draft-capital 'private, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300'; /api/league-comparison 'private, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600'.
observed: curl -D- shows no cache-control, no etag and no age header on /api/bdvm/values or /api/valuation/league-adjusted. /api/valuation/league-adjusted is a 48,555-byte league-scoped payload measured at 7,267 ms cold and 60-77 ms warm; /api/bdvm/values is up to 792 b today but is the full fundamental board once a snapshot exists. With no directive the browser applies heuristic freshness (or none), so every navigation to /rankings re-requests the overlay and the server re-serialises it.

reproduction.command: for r in /api/data /api/terminal /api/news /api/bdvm/values /api/valuation/league-adjusted; do echo "-- $r"; curl -s -D- -o /dev/null -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000$r" | grep -i '^cache-control\|^etag'; done
reproduction.expected: every route states a caching policy
reproduction.actual: /api/data, /api/terminal, /api/news all print cache-control; /api/bdvm/values and /api/valuation/league-adjusted print nothing

numericProof.formula: bytes re-sent per navigation with no policy = valuationOverlayBytes (vs 0 on a 304)

userImpact: Switching the /rankings valuation toggle back and forth, or navigating between board pages, re-downloads and re-serialises the league-adjusted overlay each time rather than revalidating for free.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers HTTP cache headers.

whatWorks: The six routes that DO set a policy set a sensible one, and /api/data additionally implements ETag + If-None-Match with a working 304 (verified: 304 in 3.1 ms, 0 bytes) and Vary: Accept-Encoding. The client-side compensation is also real — useTerminal keys its cache on valuationMode, which is the right key.
rootCause: These handlers return JSONResponse(content=...) without a headers argument, unlike their peers.
requiredRepair: Add `headers={"Cache-Control": "private, max-age=30, stale-while-revalidate=300"}` plus an ETag over the serialised body, matching /api/data. Both payloads are already versioned (paramSetId / configHash / asOf on bdvm; league factors stamp on the overlay), so a content ETag is trivially derivable.
dependencies: Note a cosmetic defect in the same area: /api/data emits `Vary: Accept-Encoding, Accept-Encoding` (duplicated token) because the header is set in two places.

title: The home page's Top Movers panel prints "No qualifying movers in this window" and a "Rank deltas vs. 30d ago" subtitle when the backend has told it there are ZERO days of history — an empty state that reads as a market fact
claimUnderTest: server.py:3385-3386 documents the distinction explicitly: "`window` is the span we ACTUALLY measured, not the span that was asked for — `windowRequested` echoes the request." The backend deliberately publishes `window`, `windowRequested` and `historyDepthDays` so a client can tell 'nothing moved' from 'nothing measured'. The frontend reads none of the three.
observed: GET /api/movers returns {"window":0,"windowRequested":14,"historyDepthDays":0,"threshold":15,"asOf":null,"risers":[],"fallers":[]}. `historyDepthDays: 0` and `asOf: null` mean the platform holds a single rank snapshot, so no delta over any window is computable. MoversPanel.jsx:201 and :217 branch only on `risers.length === 0` / `fallers.length === 0` and render 'No qualifying movers in this window.' under headings 'Risers — sell-high candidates' and 'Fallers — buy-low candidates', with the panel subtitle asserting 'Rank deltas vs. 30d ago · click a row for source breakdown'. A 30-day rank delta was never computed. MarketTicker.jsx:126 compounds it: 'Market quiet in my roster — fewer than 3 moves since last update.' Both sentences state a property of the MARKET; the true property is of our DATA. Captured verbatim from the rendered page.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/movers' ; echo ; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_probe.py /tmp/o.json && python3 -c "import json;print([r['dom']['bodyText'] for r in json.load(open('/tmp/o.json')) if r['route']=='/' and r['viewport']=='desktop'][0][:1200])"
reproduction.expected: the panel says it has no rank history, not that nobody moved
reproduction.actual: backend: historyDepthDays 0, window 0, asOf null.  page: 'RISERS — SELL-HIGH CANDIDATES / No qualifying movers in this window. / FALLERS — BUY-LOW CANDIDATES / No qualifying movers in this window.' under 'Rank deltas vs. 14d ago'

numericProof.formula: a rank delta over W days requires historyDepthDays >= W; here historyDepthDays = 0 so no window is computable, yet the UI asserts a 14/30-day comparison was made

userImpact: The user reads the most prominent movement widget on the landing page, sees both the sell-high and buy-low columns empty under a heading claiming a 30-day comparison, and concludes the dynasty market has been flat. The truth is that the platform holds one snapshot and cannot answer the question at all. The correct user action — go look at movement elsewhere, or find out why history is missing — is never prompted.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A05-F04 found the same class of error on the SIGNALS engine ('HOLD is returned for "we have no history at all" with the reason "Stable — no movement"'). This reproduces it on a different surface (MoversPanel + MarketTicker) with different code, so the class is systemic rather than local. Separately I REFUTE PRIOR-A05-F12 ('MoversPanel labels risers as buy-low and fallers as sell-high — both inverted') at HEAD e96c06ef: MoversPanel.jsx:196-199 now reads 'Risers — sell-high candidates' / 'Fallers — buy-low candidates', with an in-code note citing that finding. It is fixed.

whatWorks: The BACKEND is exemplary here and is not at fault: it separates measured window from requested window, publishes historyDepthDays and a null asOf, and its docstring explains why. Everything the frontend needs to tell the truth is already in the payload. MoversPanel's loading skeleton is also correctly sized to the settled shape (a documented fix for a ~500px layout jump).
rootCause: MoversPanel treats an empty result array as the only state worth distinguishing, and hardcodes its subtitle from the user's window selection rather than from the response's `window`.
requiredRepair: Branch on `historyDepthDays === 0 || asOf === null` first and render 'No rank history yet — we hold a single snapshot, so no movement can be measured', suppressing the subtitle's delta claim. When `window < windowRequested`, say so ('measured over N days, not 30'). Apply the same guard to MarketTicker.jsx:126. This is a display fix only — no backend change is needed.

title: The trade calculator publishes the fairness verdict "Near even" on an empty trade with zero assets on both sides
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md 'Non-Negotiable Rules' #6 — 'Call out anything mocked, bypassed, stale, duplicated, half-wired, dead, or missing'. A verdict is an assertion about a trade; with no trade there is nothing to assert.
observed: On a freshly-loaded /trade with 'No assets yet.' under both sides, Side A = 0 and Side B = 0, the sticky verdict bar renders 'Near even' with 'Gap 0' and a green-to-red gradient meter positioned at centre. verdictFromGap(gap) has no empty-trade guard: `if (Math.abs(gap) < VERDICT_NEAR_EVEN) return "Near even"` matches gap === 0 exactly as it matches a genuinely balanced trade. The two states — 'these two packages are close in value' and 'you have not built a trade' — render identically.

reproduction.expected: an empty trade shows no verdict
reproduction.actual: 'Side A 0 / No assets yet.' above a sticky bar reading 'SIDE A 0 — Near even — Gap 0 — SIDE B 0'

numericProof.formula: verdictFromGap(0) = 'Near even' because Math.abs(0) < VERDICT_NEAR_EVEN, with no guard on sideA.length + sideB.length === 0

userImpact: Low in isolation — nobody acts on an empty trade. It matters as a pattern: the same unguarded verdict function is what renders during the ~1 s window while the contract is still loading, so a shared trade link can flash 'Near even' before either side has been priced.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A02-F00 concerns the DIRECTION of the trade verdict (which side the meter calls the winner). This is the degenerate-input case and is independent.

whatWorks: The empty-list copy itself is good — 'No assets yet.' and 'Search to add to Side A…' are clear. The problem is only that the verdict bar does not respect them.
rootCause: verdictFromGap is a pure function of the gap and has no notion of an empty package; its caller renders unconditionally.
requiredRepair: Return null from verdictFromGap (or gate the sticky bar) when both sides are empty, and render a neutral 'Add assets to both sides' state.

title: DESIGN/A11Y — /rosters position-breakdown bars fail WCAG contrast at 2.19:1 in 53 places, and colour is the ONLY encoding for every segment too narrow to hold its label

codeRefs.lines: n/a — measured from the rendered DOM

claimUnderTest: design-taste-director SKILL.md product fit — 'data-dense but readable', 'mobile-friendly', 'credible for power users'. WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 (contrast 4.5:1 for text under 18.66px bold / 24px) and SC 1.4.1 (colour is not the only visual means of conveying information).
observed: Computed from the live DOM at both 1366px and 390px: 53 text nodes on /rosters fall below their required contrast ratio, of 332 sampled. The worst and most numerous are the stacked-bar segment labels — white (#ffffff) on the PICKS orange rgb(243,156,18) at 2.19:1 against a required 4.5:1, rendered at 8.96px. The same treatment covers 'PICKS 158k', 'PICKS 38k', 'PICKS 28k' and so on across all 12 team rows, plus the 'PICKS' filter chip at 12.16px. Separately: a segment only receives an inline label when it is wide enough; narrower segments (RB/TE/DL/LB/DB on most rows) render as bare coloured blocks whose ONLY identification is hue, against a 7-colour legend in which DL and LB are both purple-family and DB is teal. A user who cannot distinguish those hues cannot read those values at all — there is no tooltip, no pattern and no text alternative on the narrow segments.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_probe.py /tmp/o.json && python3 -c "import json;[print(r['route'],r['viewport'],r['dom']['contrastFailCount'],r['dom']['contrastWorst'][:3]) for r in json.load(open('/tmp/o.json')) if r['dom'].get('contrastFailCount')]"
reproduction.actual: /rosters desktop 53/332 and /rosters mobile 53/329, worst ratio 2.19 (white on rgb(243,156,18), 8.96px)

numericProof.formula: ratio = (L_light + 0.05)/(L_dark + 0.05) with relative luminance per WCAG 2.1; required 4.5 for text below 18.66px

userImpact: A power user scanning twelve rosters for positional imbalance — the page's entire purpose — cannot reliably read the segment values in bright light or on a phone, and cannot read the narrow segments at all without colour vision.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A03-F09 concerns the /rosters age-curve METHOD. No prior finding covers contrast or colour-only encoding anywhere in the product.

whatWorks: Contrast across the rest of the app is genuinely good — 12 of the 14 pages probed returned zero contrast failures at both widths. The dark palette is well constructed. (My probe also flagged one node on /league-comparison at 1.02:1, the 'Recalculate' button; the screenshot shows it rendering as a legible light chip, so I treat that single hit as a false positive of my background-walk heuristic and exclude it from the count above.)
rootCause: The bar palette was chosen for hue separation, not for contrast against white label text, and the label-visibility rule is width-driven with no fallback.
requiredRepair: Darken the orange to ~#a8620a (white on it reaches 4.9:1) or switch those labels to near-black — the amber family is the only one in the palette that white fails against. For the narrow segments, add a per-segment title/aria-label carrying 'POS value', and add a hover/tap readout so hue is never load-bearing. Reducing the seven-hue palette to four plus texture would also address the DL/LB/DB confusion the design-taste rubric warns about.

title: DESIGN — the 1-9,999 value scale is disclosed ONLY through hover tooltips (1,933 title attributes on /rankings) and appears in no visible text, so it is unreachable on every touch device
claimUnderTest: design-taste-director SKILL.md — outcomes should be 'mobile-friendly' and 'credible for power users'. CLAUDE.md's Live Value Pipeline defines a 'Common 0-9999 internal value scale', so the number 9,988 on screen is meaningless without it.
observed: The /rankings board renders VALUE as '9,988', '9,876', '9,706' with no unit and no scale on screen. The only statement of the scale is `title={`Hill-curve value ${val} (scale 1–9,999) — click for the per-source breakdown`}` on the value cell, and a second in the per-source column header info. A DOM scan of the rendered page for the string '9,999' / '9999' in visible body text returns FALSE at both 1366px and 390px. The page carries 1,933 title attributes — the disclosure layer for essentially every number on the board is hover-only. `title` never fires on touch, so on the 390px layout the scale, the meaning of the 'S+' badge beside each value, and the '14/15' sources ratio are all undiscoverable. Comparable hover-only counts elsewhere: /draft 838, /rosters 185.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_shots.py docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26 ; python3 -c "import json;[print(r['route'],r['viewport'],r['hoverOnly']['titleCount'],r['hoverOnly']['scaleStatedInVisibleText']) for r in json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/focus-hover-report.json'))]"
reproduction.expected: the scale appears in visible text on any page that prints a value
reproduction.actual: /rankings desktop titleTooltips=1933 scaleVisible=False ; /rankings mobile titleTooltips=1933 scaleVisible=False ; /draft 838 False ; /rosters 185 False

numericProof.formula: discoverability on touch = (visible-text disclosures) / (total disclosures); here 0/1933 for the value scale

userImpact: On a phone, a user reads '9,988' next to Josh Allen and '8,383' next to Joe Burrow and has no way to learn whether the gap is large or small, whether the ceiling is 9,999 or unbounded, or what unit either number is in. On /rosters the same scale is summed into a team total of '328,504' with no unit anywhere. This is the single largest comprehension gap in the product and it is invisible to desktop testing.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A01-F06 concerns the methodology panel publishing a formula that is not the live curve — a correctness problem in the explainer. This is the separate problem that the explainer is unreachable on touch at all.

whatWorks: The DESKTOP disclosure is genuinely thorough — the tooltip text is precise ('Hill-curve value N (scale 1–9,999)'), the per-source header distinguishes value-signal from rank-signal sources, and the board carries a 'How rankings work' link, a 'Methodology charts' link and an honest 'Derived from source agreement data — not predictions' caption. The rankings table also has a full <caption> and scope on all 10 <th> — the best table semantics in the app.
rootCause: Disclosure was implemented as `title` attributes, which are a desktop-only affordance, and no equivalent was added for the mobile layout.
requiredRepair: Put the scale in visible text once per board — a column subhead ('VALUE / 1–9,999') costs nothing and removes the ambiguity permanently. Replace load-bearing `title` attributes with a tap-and-hold or info-chip pattern on mobile, and give the 'S+' badge and the sources ratio a visible legend. Also note the DOM weight: 1,933 title attributes on one page is itself a parse and memory cost.

title: A11Y FUNCTIONAL — /draft has 102 unlabelled form inputs and /settings has 4 (including two range sliders that change the board), and three of the app's four data tables have no th[scope], caption or aria-label

codeRefs.lines: n/a — .draft-inline-input / .draft-money-input, measured from the rendered DOM
n/a — measured from the rendered DOM

claimUnderTest: WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 (name, role, value) and SC 1.3.1 (info and relationships). The rankings board proves the codebase already knows how to do both — it ships a <caption> and scope on all 10 <th>.
observed: Measured from the live DOM at both widths.  UNLABELLED CONTROLS (no text content, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no title, no <label for>, not wrapped in a <label>): /draft = 102, all of them `input.draft-inline-input` and `input.draft-money-input` — the per-pick team-name and dollar fields inside a 73-row auction table. A screen-reader user hears 'edit text' 102 times with nothing identifying which pick or team each belongs to. /settings = 4: two `input[type=number]` and two `input[type=range]`. The two sliders are the source-weight / TEP controls, i.e. unlabelled controls that change every value on the board.  TABLE SEMANTICS: /draft (73 rows, 14 <th>) has thScope 0, no caption, no aria-label. /settings' three tables (16/7/6 rows, 6/6/5 <th>) all have thScope 0, no caption, no aria-label. /rosters (13 rows, 4 <th>) same. Only /rankings and /finder (231 rows, 10 <th>) have scope on every header plus a caption.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_probe.py /tmp/o.json && python3 -c "import json;[print(r['viewport'],r['route'],'unlabelled',r['dom']['unlabelledCount'],'tables',r['dom']['tables']) for r in json.load(open('/tmp/o.json')) if r['dom'].get('unlabelledCount') or r['dom'].get('tables')]"
reproduction.expected: unlabelledCount 0; every data table has scoped headers and an accessible name
reproduction.actual: /draft unlabelled 102, table thScope 0/14, caption false ; /settings unlabelled 4, three tables all thScope 0 ; /rosters thScope 0/4 ; /rankings thScope 10/10 caption true

userImpact: A screen-reader user cannot operate the live auction board at all — 102 identical unnamed text fields inside an unlabelled 73-row grid gives no way to know which pick is being edited. On /settings the same user can move two sliders with no idea what they control, and those sliders re-rank the entire board.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding in the 531-item index addresses form labelling or table semantics.

whatWorks: The app-wide accessibility baseline is better than most: every one of the 14 pages probed has lang="en", exactly one <h1>, a <main> landmark, a working skip-link, and zero images missing alt (188 player headshots on /rankings, all with alt). PlayerImage.jsx additionally sets loading="lazy" and decoding="async" with a three-stage graceful fallback. /rankings and /finder are a model for the other tables. Zero horizontal page overflow at 390px on all 14 pages, with every wide table correctly wrapped in an overflow-x:auto container.
rootCause: The rankings table was built with semantics in mind; the later tables and the draft board's inline editors were not, and there is no lint rule or test asserting the invariant.
requiredRepair: Add aria-label to each draft inline input naming its pick and field ('Pick 1.05 team', 'Pick 1.05 dollars'), add scope="col" to every <th> and a <caption> (or aria-label) to the /draft, /settings and /rosters tables, and add visible <label> elements to the two /settings sliders and two number inputs. Then add an eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y rule so the invariant is enforced rather than re-audited.

title: DESIGN/MOBILE — at 390px the trade calculator's sticky verdict bar is clipped by a floating action button, /draft's teams panel refuses to stack, and /rankings' edge-summary chips truncate to unusable stubs

codeRefs.lines: n/a — sticky verdict bar, measured from a 390x844 render
n/a — 'Teams & budgets' panel, measured from a 390x844 render
n/a — Edge summary chips, measured from a 390x844 render

claimUnderTest: design-taste-director SKILL.md — 'strengthen thumb-zone controls and persistent actions on mobile', 'data-dense but readable'. CLAUDE.md Performance Rules — 'Prioritize page-load speed and perceived responsiveness'.
observed: Three distinct 390px defects, each captured in a screenshot.  (1) /trade: the sticky bottom verdict bar renders 'SIDE A / 0 / [meter] / Near even / Gap 0 / SID' — Side B's label is cut to 'SID' and its number is overlapped by a floating circular action button anchored bottom-right. The bar is the calculator's primary readout and half of it is unreadable.  (2) /draft: the 'Teams & budgets' panel lays out a heading column beside a full-width 'Load from Draft Capital' button and does not stack; the description wraps one or two words per line ('Budgets pre-' / 'fill from' / 'the live' / 'Draft' / 'Capital'), producing a five-line ragged column ~90px wide.  (3) /rankings: the Edge summary cards clip their content to '#244 E…' / 'Sell +…' / '#202 De…' / 'Sell…' — the player is unidentifiable and the magnitude is gone, so the panel conveys only that a signal exists. The 'FLAGGED — NEEDS CAUTION' heading is itself cut mid-word by the same floating button.  None of these produces page-level horizontal overflow (documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth on all 14 pages, which is why a scroll-based check misses them entirely).

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_shots.py docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26   # inspect trade-mobile.png, draft-mobile.png, rankings-mobile.png
reproduction.expected: no clipped labels or single-word wrap columns at 390px
reproduction.actual: trade-mobile.png shows 'SID' + occluded Side B total; draft-mobile.png shows a 5-line single-word column; rankings-mobile.png shows '#244 E…' / 'Sell +…'

numericProof.formula: page-level scrollWidth > clientWidth detects 0 of these 3 defects, because each clips WITHIN a fixed-position or flex container rather than overflowing the document

userImpact: On /trade the user cannot read what the other side of their own trade is worth — on the surface most likely to be used on a phone, mid-negotiation. On /rankings the edge summary, which exists to name buy and sell candidates, names none of them.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding addresses mobile layout.

whatWorks: The mobile shell is otherwise strong and clearly deliberate: a five-item bottom tab bar (Home/Ranks/Trade/News/Menu) in the thumb zone, zero horizontal page overflow on all 14 pages at 390px, every wide table wrapped in its own overflow-x:auto container so the page body never scrolls sideways, and the /rankings board correctly reflows from a 1,278px table to a 578px one. The stat-tile grid reflows cleanly to two columns.
rootCause: The floating action button is positioned over the sticky bar's right edge with no reserved gutter; the /draft panel uses a row flex with no stacking breakpoint; the edge chips use fixed-width truncation rather than reflowing to two lines.
requiredRepair: Reserve right padding on the sticky trade bar equal to the FAB's footprint (or move the FAB above the bar); add a flex-direction:column breakpoint below ~520px to the /draft teams panel; let the edge-summary chips wrap to two lines on narrow viewports so the player name and the magnitude both survive.

title: A11Y — 8 of the first 22 keyboard tab stops on /draft have no visible focus indicator (no outline, no box-shadow); /trade has 3 and /rosters 2

codeRefs.lines: n/a — no :focus-visible rule reaches these controls

claimUnderTest: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7 (focus visible). The rest of the app passes, so this is a gap rather than an absent system.
observed: Walking Tab 22 times from document start and reading getComputedStyle on document.activeElement at each stop: /draft at 390px has 8 stops where outlineStyle begins 'none' AND boxShadow is empty or 'none'; /trade at 390px has 3; /rosters at 1366px has 2. The same walk on /rankings (both widths), /draft at 1366px, /league-comparison and / returns 0 — so the default focus treatment does exist and works, and these are controls that override it. Focus ORDER itself was sane on every page walked: no stop landed on a zero-size or off-screen element.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_shots.py docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26 ; python3 -c "import json;[print(r['route'],r['viewport'],r['noFocusRing'],'/22') for r in json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/focus-hover-report.json'))]"
reproduction.actual: /draft mobile 8/22 ; /trade mobile 3/22 ; /rosters desktop 2/22 ; every other combination 0/22

numericProof.formula: a stop fails when getComputedStyle(el).outlineStyle starts with 'none' and boxShadow is empty or 'none'

userImpact: A keyboard-only user tabbing through the live draft board loses track of where they are 8 times in the first 22 stops — on the page where a mistaken keystroke costs a draft pick.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers keyboard focus. Rated medium because my detector only reads outline and box-shadow; a control indicating focus purely via a background-colour change would be a false positive here.

whatWorks: Focus order is correct everywhere walked, the skip-link is present and first on all 14 pages, and 5 of the 8 page/viewport combinations walked have a visible ring on all 22 stops.
rootCause: Specific controls (draft inline inputs, trade chips) reset outline without substituting an equivalent indicator.
requiredRepair: Add a global `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }` that these components do not override, and remove the local outline:none resets.

title: A11Y/MOBILE — 873 of 900 interactive targets on /rankings at 390px are under 44px, and type as small as 9.0px ships on three pages

codeRefs.lines: n/a — row-level interactive cells, measured from a 390x844 render

claimUnderTest: design-taste-director SKILL.md — 'strengthen thumb-zone controls and persistent actions on mobile'. WCAG 2.1 SC 2.5.5 (Target Size, AAA) sets 44x44 CSS px; SC 2.5.8 (AA, 2.2) sets 24x24 as the floor.
observed: Measured on visible, non-zero-size interactive elements (a[href], button, input, select, textarea, role=button/tab/link, tabindex>=0) at 390x844: /rankings 873 small of 900 total, /finder 873 of 900, /draft 373 of 475, /settings 39 of 126, /rosters 31 of 63. At 1366px the counts are similar (/rankings 891 of 900), so this is a row-density decision rather than a responsive-layout failure. The bulk on /rankings and /finder is the per-row player/value/source cells, which are clickable (they open the popup and the per-source breakdown) but sized for information density. Separately, computed font sizes below 11px appear on /rankings (9.0, 9.2, 9.3, 9.9, 10.6, 10.9), /finder (same set), /rosters (9.0, 9.3, 9.6, 9.9), /settings (9.3, 10.2, 10.6, 10.9) and /league (9.9, 10.2, 10.4, 10.6, 10.9) — 9.0px on a 390px phone.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_probe.py /tmp/o.json && python3 -c "import json;[print(r['viewport'],r['route'],r['dom']['smallTargetCount'],'/',r['dom']['interactiveCount'],r['dom']['tinyFontSizes']) for r in json.load(open('/tmp/o.json')) if r['viewport']=='mobile']"
reproduction.expected: interactive targets >= 44px in at least one dimension; no type below 11px

userImpact: Tapping a specific player row on a phone is error-prone, and the 9px metadata (team, age, spread) is at the edge of legibility on a 390px screen for anyone without perfect near vision.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers touch targets or type scale.

whatWorks: The pages that are NOT dense tables get this right: /terminal 4 small of 26, /bdvm 7 of 29, /waivers 9 of 31, /market/sharp-roster-percentage 11 of 33. The bottom tab bar targets are correctly sized. So the small-target problem is confined to the board rows and is a deliberate density trade, not an oversight everywhere.
rootCause: The rankings row is a desktop-density table reflowed to mobile without a distinct mobile row treatment, so every cell keeps its desktop height.
requiredRepair: This is the one finding here where the fix is a design decision, not a bug fix. Recommendation, per the design-taste rubric: give /rankings a distinct mobile row — a two-line card at ~56px with rank+name+position on line one and value+confidence+edge on line two, one tap target per row instead of eight, and raise the metadata type floor to 11px. That is a deliberate density reduction, so it should be a stated decision rather than a silent change; keep the current dense table available behind the existing 'Columns' control for power users.

title: _LEAGUE_CONTEXT_CACHE is a single global slot with no league key, so every league's rookie-anchor roster count and TE bonus come from the default league
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md 'Rule for new code' — 'Need rosters / teams / matchups? -> resolve via leagueKey. One pipeline per league. Never collapse.' roster_count is a per-league property (team count) and bonus_rec_te is a per-league scoring property.
observed: `_LEAGUE_CONTEXT_CACHE = {"context": None, "fetched_at": 0.0}` is a single-slot dict with a 1-hour TTL and NO league dimension. `_resolve_league_context()` takes no league argument at all — it resolves the id via `league_registry.get_sleeper_league_id()`, which returns the DEFAULT league, then caches the result globally. Any second league on the same scoring profile with a different team count or TE bonus reads the default league's numbers from this cache. The cache is also read-before-write with the fetch outside any lock, so concurrent cold misses each hit Sleeper.

reproduction.expected: cache keyed by league (or by scoring profile, with the league-specific parts excluded)

numericProof.formula: distinct values servable = cacheSlots = 1, while distinct correct values required = leaguesInRegistry

userImpact: Only realised on a multi-league deployment where the two leagues differ in team count or TE premium; today both live leagues share scoring_profile superflex_tep15_ppr1, so the observable impact is latent. Reported because the audit brief asks explicitly whether each cache key includes the league key, and this one does not.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A20-F03 found a related shape in gameplan — 'scoringFit and receptionFit are measured against a Sleeper league that is not in the registry, then cached per league key as if they were'. Same family (a league-scoped quantity cached without the right key), different module. Rated medium because the impact is latent on the current single-scoring-profile registry.

whatWorks: The function's degradation path is correct and well documented — a fallback dict with fetched_from_sleeper: False is returned on any failure rather than raising, so the pipeline produces output offline, and the flag makes the fallback visible to callers. By contrast, the caches that DO get keying right are numerous: _OVERRIDES_RESPONSE_CACHE keys on (body hash, view, leagueKey, sleeper_matches) and deliberately refuses to cache the leagueAdjusted path at all; _OVERLAY_RESPONSE_CACHE keys on (kind, leagueKey, loadedLeague, view, sleeper_matches) with the freshness stamp inside the value; gameplan's _BUNDLE_CACHE keys on league_key plus a source stamp rather than a clock; _DRAFT_CAPITAL_CACHE keys on league key.
rootCause: The function predates multi-league support and was never given a league parameter when the registry landed.
requiredRepair: Give _resolve_league_context a league_key parameter and key the cache dict on it, defaulting to the registry default so existing callers are unaffected.

title: Three documented payload/page claims are measurably wrong: '~4 MB uncompressed' (is 11.95 MB), '~90% byte reduction' (is 38%), and 'frontend/app/ ... terminal/' (the directory does not exist and /terminal is a 404)
claimUnderTest: (1) CLAUDE.md: 'view=full (default, backward-compat): returns the full canonical contract (~4 MB uncompressed...)'. (2) server.py:3126-3128 and frontend/app/api/dynasty-data/route.js:45: compact is a '~90% byte reduction' / '~90% smaller'. (3) CLAUDE.md directory listing: 'frontend/ ... app/ # rankings/, trade/, draft/, bdvm/, waivers/, terminal/, news/, settings/, login/'.
observed: (1) The full contract measures 11,953,535 bytes uncompressed — 2.99x the documented ~4 MB. (2) compact measures 7,363,760 bytes against full's 11,953,535, a 38.4% reduction, not 90%; and it is 13.0% LARGER than the view desktop requests (see W26-F001). (3) `ls frontend/app/terminal` returns 'No such file or directory'; the directory listing shows no terminal entry; grep finds no link to '/terminal' anywhere in frontend source. Loading http://127.0.0.1:3000/terminal in a browser renders the app shell around Next's 'This page could not be found.' — and still downloads 12,481,320 decoded bytes of player contract to do it (see W26-F002). The /api/terminal ENDPOINT is live and is correctly consumed by the home page, so only the page claim is false.

reproduction.actual: full=11953535 ; compact=7363760 ; ls: cannot access 'frontend/app/terminal': No such file or directory

userImpact: None directly on a user. It matters because the '~90%' figure is the stated justification for routing mobile devices to that view, and it is what makes W26-F001 look like a non-problem to a reader of the code.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A10-F09 established the pattern ('CLAUDE.md declares defect D-2 resolved while the code it cites says the opposite'). These are three further instances. The '~4 MB' figure and the compact-vs-app inversion were both pre-noted in evidence/perf/api-data-payload-sizes.txt; this finding supplies the mechanism and the third instance.

whatWorks: The vast majority of CLAUDE.md's technical claims that I tested held up, including the scoring-profile vs leagueKey split, the ETag/304 behaviour, the single-flight design of the overlay and overrides caches, the /league public-data exemption in AppShell, and the fact that view=array carries no legacy players dict.
rootCause: The figures were written before the contract grew and were never re-measured; the terminal page was removed or renamed without updating the directory listing.
requiredRepair: Re-measure and correct the three figures. If /terminal is meant to exist, note that /api/terminal is live and consumed by the home page, so only the page is missing; otherwise remove it from the directory listing.
